"Our second approach is based on the ground-state path integral form of AFQMC, but introduces several advances, including accelerated sampling (...) by a dynamic force bias [27], which enables global moves of fields on a time slice with acceptance ratio of over 90% (...) With this approach, our calculations typically have beta ~ 320 or larger (in units of t^-1), discretized with over 12,800 time-slices." (...) "In both approaches, the computational cost scales as ~ Ns N^2 beta." (...) "Computing was carried out at the Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory (...) and at the computational facilities at the College of William and Mary."

compute.note: This row is a VarBench reference calculation (dataset arXiv:2302.04919; code link in the row reference) that cites PRA 92, 033603 as the AFQMC method paper; the PRA paper does not contain this lattice/filling and its beta ~ 320 / 12,800 time-slice / OLCF statements refer to its own cold-atom calculations. Cost-relevant inputs come from the published VarBench AFQMCLAB parameter files: samples = measureSweep (200 Metropolis measurement sweeps at dt = 0.01); timesliceSize 3600 at dt = 0.01 (imaginary-time length = dt x timesliceSize). No walker counts beyond these inputs, no core counts, core-hours or wall-clock are stated anywhere.

corrections.reason: The cited paper did not produce the number and does not contain it: PRA 92, 033603 is the method paper, attached two years after the upload in answer to a request for 'a paper describing the AFQMC method with negative U' (PR #23 thread). The energy is VarBench's own computation, run by co-author Yiqi Yang (Zhang group) with AFQMCLAB and described in the VarBench paper's Suppl. S3 E 1-2. Same history and same fix as the sibling repulsive row Hubbard/square_64_P_32_8 AFQMC -33.642(5), whose reference was changed to the Science paper under the 2026-09-21 ruling (option a, corrections.mjs 'FP4-arxiv-2507-02644#2'); this entry applies that precedent to the eleven rows listed in qmbl-verify DECISIONS.md section 1 as '11 Hubbard (PRA 92, 033603) | the cited paper is a dilute continuum gas study', whose ruling (2026-09-16) was on hold because 'the premise is not established'; the PR #23 exchange (the uploader naming PRA 92 as the method paper) and the VarBench SM's own description of these runs establish it. This is a reference change only, not the rejected baseline/contributed flag. Energy, sigma and bound_type stay: the run is sign-problem-free (N_up = N_dn = 128 in the trial determinant), at dt = 0.01 which the VarBench SM states was verified against the statistical error, so exact (stochastic) with its sigma. Independent check: Particle-hole identity: -1158.261(15) + 8 x 128 = -134.261(15) against Qin et al. Table IV, 16 x 16, U = 8, PBC: '-134.23(3)': 0.92 sigma combined. M5 agrees.
